clips.speaker: Stephanie Lung
clips.title: StashAway首席配置官：科技七巨头陷入“无人区”，前景存疑
title_lines: 科技七巨头陷入“无人区”

subtitles.en: Why do you think we're seeing a massive pullback right now in specifically mag seven? And would you buy that dip specifically?
subtitles.zh: 为什么你认为科技七巨头现在出现大幅回调？你会趁低买入吗？

subtitles.en: Yeah. I think, if you look at a mag seven this year, I think as you've shown in the chart just now, I mean, they have really underperformed. So when we look at, for example, during the first half, S&P was actually up around 10%, but the mag seven was flat. So the rest of the 493 actually outperformed the mag seven significantly in the past six months.
subtitles.zh: 是的，今年科技七巨头表现落后。上半年标普500上涨约10%，但七巨头基本持平。其他493只股票过去六个月显著跑赢七巨头。

subtitles.en: And a lot of that of course was trimmed by the AI hardware names, but like half of that also was trimmed by the broader market. So I think if you think about the mag seven, of course, they were the darlings of the last decade or so. And it was the era of social media. It was the era of cloud. Now we're moving on to the era of AI. And as we look at kind of broader index, even if you look at S&P during different periods, different leaderships.
subtitles.zh: 其中一部分是AI硬件股拖累，但另一半是整体市场因素。七巨头曾是过去十年的宠儿，那是社交媒体和云计算的年代。现在进入AI时代，标普500在不同时期有不同的领涨板块。

subtitles.en: So I think the question mark is, okay, is like companies like Open AI and Frappe are going to become the more important companies compared to the mag seven. And in particular, again, the mag seven right now is spending a lot of CapEx before, I mean, it offers a lot of safety for investors, a lot of cash flow. Now that it's being put in a question mark, so I mean, mag seven right now, if you compare it to the best growth companies, they're not the highest in growth. If you compare the safest companies, they're not the safest ones. So there's kind of a, it's somewhere in between in No Man's Land, I would say. So I mean, I think that's a that's a question mark going forward for for mag seven as a whole.
subtitles.zh: 问题是，像OpenAI和Frappe这样的公司是否会比七巨头更重要？七巨头目前资本开支巨大，过去提供安全性和现金流，但现在这些优势存疑。与最佳成长股比，它们成长性不足；与最安全股票比，它们安全性不够。可以说它们处于“无人区”。这是七巨头整体面临的问题。

clips.speaker: Stephanie Lung
clips.title: 英特尔回报路径清晰：谷歌可见度低，AI硬件分化将如何影响配置？
title_lines: AI硬件分化将如何影响配置？
title_highlights: AI硬件分化将如何影响配置？

subtitles.en: Stephanie Rebecca here, I just want to pick up on the point that Dave was making, kind of that short term versus longer term view. When we think about these shifts here, you mentioned that pullback that we've seen in AI hardware, some of that rotation elsewhere, healthcare, and so on. I'm just trying to get a sense. Do you see that as a durable shift? Or is this a moment, a transient moment of profit taking?
subtitles.zh: 我想接着Dave的话题，关于短期与长期视角。你提到AI硬件回调，资金轮动到医疗等其他板块。这是持久转变还是暂时的获利了结？

subtitles.en: Yeah, so if we look at what's going to ultimately drive long-term returns, I mean, it's obviously earnings growth. And still, I mean, where you find the best earnings growth is within the AI kind of value chain. Now, of course, at different times, different by parts of the AI value chain offers you most visibility in terms of return on investment. Right now, it's still hardware.
subtitles.zh: 长期回报最终由盈利增长驱动。目前盈利增长最好的地方仍在AI价值链中。当然，不同时期AI价值链的不同部分投资回报可见度不同。目前仍是硬件。

subtitles.en: And I think last night's earnings actually clearly shown that, for example, Intel has a very, very clear kind of path to seeing returns, whereas hyper-scalers like Google has a low visibility. So I still think that that remains kind of the core of the overall kind of bull market. But of course, you see kind of bolts of volatile periods right now we're in one and investors naturally rotate into other saver sectors or sectors that kind of are in favor.
subtitles.zh: 昨晚的财报清楚显示，英特尔有非常明确的回报路径，而谷歌等超大规模企业可见度较低。所以我仍认为这是整体牛市的核心。但当前处于波动期，投资者自然会轮动到更安全的板块。

subtitles.en: But I think over long-term, basically, if you look at fundamental, that's still very strong. US economy is still growing very strongly. Of course, we have a slight inflation problem. But it is through these times when you are in inflationary growth where equities tend to perform quite well. But as investors, actually, we don't have to think about the short term necessarily.
subtitles.zh: 但长期基本面依然强劲。美国经济仍在强劲增长，当然有轻微通胀问题。但在通胀性增长时期，权益资产往往表现不错。投资者其实不必过于关注短期。

subtitles.en: And we've actually done quite a bit of work on regular investing recently that compares quite favorably with the market timer, which I'm happy to kind of talk about more. Yeah, I want to pick up on that. I know you've done a lot of this research into sort of dollar cost averaging. And essentially, when is the right moment for the investor to lean in to just talk us through your thesis there and what you've found?
subtitles.zh: 我们最近做了不少关于定期投入的研究，结果优于择时交易。我很乐意多谈谈。我知道你们做了很多关于定投的研究，投资者何时应该加大投入？请讲讲你的观点和发现。

clips.title: StashAway首席配置官：定期投入优于择时，中国市场同样适用

subtitles.en: Yeah, I mean, that's something very interesting work recently. And next week, we're going to publish our periodical monthly sales insights that talks about that. And basically, the insight that we've found is what we're trying to compare is, let's say for investors who buys at every dip of 10% dip, 20% dip, 30% dip, how does that compare to somebody who just invest regularly? Let's say on a monthly basis.
subtitles.zh: 这是我们最近一项有趣的研究。下周我们将发布月度销售洞察。我们比较了两种策略：一种是每次下跌10%、20%、30%时买入，另一种是每月定期投入。

subtitles.en: I think intuitively, you would think that actually the investor who can buy on a dip on every dip would beat the regular investor. But in reality, when we ran the numbers, the regular investors actually win both of the time and buy a pretty wide margin over five years, 10 year, 15 year time Verizon. And I think the reason behind that is actually quite logical. So if you think about the dip buyer, they have to wait for the dip. But actually, bull markets run a lot longer than the bear markets. So you have to wait for a long time in that dip to come.
subtitles.zh: 直觉上，每次下跌都买入的投资者应该跑赢定期投入者。但实际数据表明，定期投入者在5年、10年、15年维度上始终胜出，且优势明显。原因很合理：下跌买入者必须等待下跌，但牛市持续时间远长于熊市，等待下跌的成本很高。

subtitles.en: And by waiting, that's actually the most expensive game in a market because you lose out to all those games. The underlying premise there is there needs to be a sustain bull market. Yes. Does that apply in a market like China, where it's always tactical and the index would be at the same level periodically over the period of 20 years at about the same level, where it's a different set of opportunities. How does it work in China?
subtitles.zh: 等待是市场上最昂贵的游戏，因为你会错过所有涨幅。但前提是存在持续牛市。在中国这样的市场，指数20年来基本持平，机会不同，定投策略是否适用？

subtitles.en: So I mean, even if you look at China, it's arguably perhaps one of the worst performing markets in recent years. I mean, the total return is still positive. So if you get the dividends, etc., that's still like a, we're sloping line. The slope is, of course, less steep than the US market. So if you were to dollar cost average in China, probably your gains would be lower than that in the US. But still, I mean, you make out for that volatility exactly because you dollar cost average. Not just price, yeah, absolutely.
subtitles.zh: 即使是中国，近年表现相对较弱，但总回报仍为正。加上股息等，收益曲线仍是向上倾斜的，只是斜率小于美国市场。在中国做定投，收益可能低于美国，但正是通过定投，你从波动中获益，而不仅仅是价格。

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
